Northgate Reuse Center
Home / Donate Goods / Pickup Service
Our pickup service lets donors pass on usable furnishings they no longer need to local schools, youth clubs, and neighborhood associations. The table below shows what we can and cannot collect.
Accepted | Not accepted |
Desks and filing cabinets | Household sofas and beds |
Meeting tables and chairs | Built-in shelving |
Storage shelving and carts | Kitchen appliances |
Whiteboards and partitions | Broken or damaged items |
To arrange a pickup, follow these steps:
1. Send us an itemized list of the pieces, with approximate sizes.
2. Our staff review the list.
3. We confirm a pickup date within three business days.
Conditions: A pickup is arranged only if a load contains 12 items or more. The site must have ground-floor loading access and a reserved parking space. Pickups run Monday through Friday, 9:00 A.M. to 4:00 P.M. An outside moving crew does all lifting.
There is no charge for the service, and proof of purchase is not needed. Items cannot be brought to us, as no drop-off point is available.

Attendee Changes: Trade and Industry Forum
This page is for anyone who holds a paid place at this year's Trade and Industry Forum, with or without a workshop seat, and can no longer attend. Fees are not refunded, and no places remain for sale. Rather than leave the seat empty, you may name a colleague to attend in your place. --[1]--
Naming Someone Else

The person replacing you takes over the main program sessions and the daily lunches in your booking. Two kinds of extras are treated differently. Workshop seats and evening dinner tickets stay with your own booking and must be reserved again by your replacement.
Common Questions
May I name someone from another company?
No. Only a colleague from your own organization qualifies.
Will a workshop seat be held for my replacement?
No. Seats are limited, and we cannot promise that a free one remains.

To: All installation crews
From: Helen Mortimer, Installation Supervisor
Date: February 27
Subject: Completion images and billing
From Monday, March 6, closing out a job will include one new step: photographing the finished work at the customer's home and sending the images to the office.
The change comes after several accounts went unpaid for weeks over the past four months because customers questioned marks and missing pieces that we could not account for once the crew had left. Some of you have called this extra paperwork at the end of a long day, and I understand that, but we have nothing to show what we handed over. Every van already carries a tablet, so no new equipment is needed.
Each set must show the following:
[1] the whole row of units with every door and drawer closed
[2] the joint where the counter meets the wall
[3] the base panels along the floor
[4] the inside of one upper unit with its shelves in place
[5] the floor and walls beside the finished units
On jobs of more than twelve units, add a wide view from the opposite corner. A sample set has already been circulated to crew leaders.
The images must be uploaded before the van comes back in. The office cannot release the bill for a job until the record is on file, so a set that arrives the next morning holds up payment. Staff here will match each set to the invoice.
To begin with, the step applies for four weeks only to the three crews at the north yard, where Culver Timber Supply will keep delivering materials to each address as before. Crew leaders in that group will check every set before it is sent. When the four weeks are up, the remaining crews will hear from me about a short training session. If customers continue to raise questions after that, we may ask for a signature on site as well.
This notice is posted in the tool room. Each crew leader must add initials beside the crew number.

To all floor wardens:
Two tenant firms have taken additional space since December, and far more people now work on the second and fourth floors than when the present stairway assignments were drawn up. The exercise on March 20 will show whether those assignments still empty the building within the eight-minute target. The exercise required each year under our safety certificate was completed in October, so this run is an additional one.
Each warden clears the areas listed against their zone and then leaves by the stairway shown on the attached sheet. Zones move in the order of the start times printed there, and no group should enter a stairway ahead of its own slot.
Reminder: the standing exception for Zone C applies to this run as well. Its wave begins after the other three so that visitors attending courses can be given instructions before they are moved.
Yvette Twomey will observe from the ground floor and will time each wave. Please hand her your completed zone tally within one business day. Her report will decide whether any assignment is changed before the next run.
Duncan Mulvaney

Observation report — sheet EV-1450, run of March 20
Observer role: timekeeper and independent observer
Vantage point: ground-floor lobby desk, then the rear yard gate
Three of the four waves ran as allocated. The reception level and mail room group left the floor inside its slot, and the name list it handed in was complete and correct. The fourth-floor call center group was standing at its assembly point well before the end of its interval, the widest margin of the four groups. The third-floor training rooms and file room group began at the approved later time and finished inside its interval.
Movement was held up in two places. The second-floor group set off promptly, but the North Stair carried an unbroken line from the second floor to the ground for almost the whole interval, and the last of the group reached the yard about three minutes past its allocated time. On the East Stair, the ground-floor door was propped open only after the first group using that stair had reached it, which cost that group about forty seconds.
For the next run, the second-floor zone should be divided between the North Stair and the East Stair, with the two halves starting a minute apart.
Y. T.

Brackenridge Energy Services
Workplace Energy Review
Brackenridge Energy Services carries out workplace energy reviews at no charge, showing businesses where their premises could use less gas and electricity.
To enter, send us the entry form with twelve months of meter readings, and we will confirm your place within three business days. Our survey team of two then spends one day on site, guided by a member of your staff. Four weeks after the visit, we mail you a written summary ranking the measures we recommend.
We can review premises only if their meters are registered in your name, not billed through a landlord or shared supply. You must also have occupied them for two years or more, and they must remain in use for a year after the visit. Each company may enter one property per round. Our team can also write an action plan on site for an optional $250.
Each round has its own entry deadline and review week:
Entries by March 6 — review week of April 13
Entries by May 1 — review week of June 8
